title: Business Central Case Study: How World Emblem Automated High-Volume Manufacturing Processes
summary: World Emblem, a high-volume manufacturing company, demonstrates how strategic automation and configuration-based customizations in Business Central enabled them to quadruple revenue without proportionally increasing headcount. By converting tribal knowledge into system-based rules and migrating legacy logic into Business Central, they improved scalability, reduced bottlenecks, and created a more maintainable operation.
key_points: Converting manual decision-making into configuration tables creates business independence and reduces the need for custom development cycles
Migrating business logic from external systems into Business Central improves maintainability and reduces support overhead
Strategic automation of high-volume processes (4,000 - 5,000 invoices daily) allows employees to focus on value-added work rather than routine tasks
Partnering with a vendor who understands industry-specific requirements and prioritizes client self-sufficiency over dependency yields better long-term results
